issues.legal_issue: A post-assessment intimation from an authorized audit body identifying an error in the application of law can constitute information permitting reassessment, even if the officer could have discovered the correct legal position during the original assessment.
material_facts: The officer assessed income from properties that were self-occupied and allowed a deduction for municipal taxes, although the deduction was not admissible under the applicable rule for determining annual value.
After the assessment, the audit department informed the officer that the deduction had been wrongly allowed as a matter of law.
The officer relied on that intimation and formed the view that income had escaped assessment, then issued a reassessment notice.
The officer had known during the original assessment that the properties were self-occupied.
issues.conclusion: The audit department's intimation constituted information, and the officer was entitled to reopen the assessment; the appeal was allowed and the notice was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 147(b) of the Income-tax Act, the officer must receive information after the original assessment and, in consequence of it, have reason to believe that taxable income escaped assessment. Information may concern facts or law. Information is not disqualified merely because the officer could have obtained it earlier through diligent inquiry. An authorized audit body may scrutinize assessments and identify errors of law, and its intimation may be information for this purpose. Section 148 was the basis for the notice, and section 23(2) governed the annual valuation at issue. The Court relied on Maharaj Kumar Kamal Singh v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bihar and Orissa; R. B. Bansilal Abirchand Firm v. Commissioner of Income Tax, M.P.; Assistant Controller of Estate Duty, Hyderabad v. Nawab Sir Mir Osman Ali Khan Bahadur; and Commissioner of Income-tax, Gujarat v. A. Raman & Co. It approved Commissioner of Income-tax, Delhi v. H. H. Smt. Chand Kanwarji, Commissioner of Income-tax v. Kelukutty, and Vashist Bhargava v. Income-tax Officer, Salary Circle, New Delhi.

rule.if: reassessment_proceeding and information_received_after_assessment and audit_note_identifies_legal_error and audit_body_authorized_to_scrutinize_assessments and officer_believes_income_escaped

predicates.reassessment_proceeding: An officer is seeking to reopen an earlier tax assessment.
predicates.information_received_after_assessment: The officer received information after completing the earlier assessment.
predicates.audit_note_identifies_legal_error: An audit body informed the officer that the earlier assessment applied the law incorrectly.
predicates.audit_body_authorized_to_scrutinize_asse: The body that supplied the information was authorized to scrutinize assessments and identify legal errors.
predicates.officer_believes_income_escaped: In consequence of the information, the officer formed a belief that taxable income had escaped assessment.

issues.definition: When an officer seeks to reopen an assessment on the basis of a later audit note identifying a legal error, the note comes from an authorized scrutiny body, and the officer consequently believes taxable income escaped assessment, reopening is permitted.
